exposure: Intact perineum/1st degree spontaneous perineal tear
cohort: Post-partum women in Nigeria who experienced vaginal births were categorized into three groups based on the extent of perineal trauma: OASIS, episiotomy/2nd degree tear, or intact perineum/1st degree tear.
finding: Obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) following vaginal birth are associated with significantly increased risks of urinary incontinence and anal incontinence, as well as reduced quality of life, compared to less severe perineal trauma or intact perineum.
mod_finding: The study focuses on complications of vaginal birth, but does not compare outcomes related to mode of birth (e.g., vaginal birth vs. C-section).
birth_weight: N/A (macrosomia mentioned as a risk factor for OASIS, but not a general inclusion criterion for cohort)
